_about: Translator notes: dotted key -> what the string is for, length limits, what the {placeholders} are. Keys not listed here are plain sentences for kids aged 6 to 12.
layout.titleHome: Browser tab title of the home page. Keep "Oomba Academy" as is: the brand stays in Latin letters, untranslated.
layout.titleWith: Browser tab title of every other page. {title} is the page name, e.g. a game title. Keep "Oomba Academy" as is: the brand stays in Latin letters, untranslated.
layout.description: Meta description for search engines and link previews, max ~150 chars.
layout.skip: Hidden link for keyboard users that jumps past the menu to the page content.
layout.mainNav: Screen-reader name of the main menu (the navigation landmark).
layout.signIn: Button/tab label, max ~10 chars (it fits under an icon in the phone tab bar).
layout.meLabel: Screen-reader label of the profile button. {name} is the player's display name.
layout.back: Back link at the top of inner pages, max ~12 chars.
layout.badgeNew: Screen-reader text for the red number badge on a menu tab. {count} is a number.
layout.search.placeholder: Placeholder in the search box in the header, max ~26 chars.
layout.lang.title: Heading of the language menu (the 🌐 button).
layout.lang.button: Screen-reader label of the 🌐 button. {language} is the current language's own name, e.g. "Français".
layout.theme.title: Heading of the theme menu (the ☀️/🌙/🌓 button next to 🌐): light or dark colours for the site.
layout.theme.button: Screen-reader label of the theme button. {theme} is one of layout.theme.system, .light or .dark.
layout.theme.system: Theme choice that follows the phone or computer's own light/dark setting. Short, max ~24 chars.
layout.theme.light: Theme choice: light colours (dark text on a light screen). One word.
layout.theme.dark: Theme choice: dark colours (light text on a dark screen). One word.
layout.footer.tagline: Footer line. Keep "Oomba Academy" as is: the brand stays in Latin letters, untranslated.
layout.footer.parents: Footer link to the page for parents, teachers and carers.
layout.footer.builders: Footer link to the game SDK page for kids who build games.
nav.home: Menu tab, max ~8 chars (phone tab bar, under an emoji).
nav.search: Menu tab, max ~8 chars (phone tab bar, under an emoji).
nav.build: Menu tab, max ~8 chars (phone tab bar, under an emoji). Means "make a game".
nav.friends: Menu tab, max ~8 chars (phone tab bar, under an emoji).
nav.me: Menu tab for your own account/profile, max ~8 chars.
errors.notFound.heading: Playful heading on the 404 page (kid reading level).
errors.api.slowDown: Shown when someone taps or sends too fast (rate limit).
errors.api.crossSite: Technical error, rarely seen. Plain translation is fine.
time.justNow: Relative time for something less than a minute ago. Other "5 minutes ago" texts come from the browser's own Intl formatting.
cards.new: Shown instead of stars on a game card when nobody has rated it yet, max ~6 chars.
cards.starsLabel: Screen-reader label for a star rating. {stars} is like "4.5", {count} is the number of ratings.
cards.playing: Small pill on a game cover: how many people play it right now. {count} is a number. Keep it very short.
cards.gameBy: Screen-reader label of a game card. {title} is the game title (not translated), {name} the builder's name.
cards.by: Under a game title: who made it. {name} is a username.
cards.plays: How many times a game was played. {count} is the exact number (for choosing the plural form), {n} is the same number already shortened, like "1.2K". Show {n}.
cards.seeAll: Link at the end of a row of games, max ~10 chars.
cards.scrollBack: Screen-reader label of the arrow button that scrolls a row of games back. {title} is the row name, e.g. "Popular".
cards.scrollForward: Screen-reader label of the arrow button that scrolls a row of games forward. {title} is the row name.
vis.private: Who can play a game: only the builder. Short, shown after 🔒.
vis.friends: Who can play a game: the builder's friends. Short, shown after 👫.
vis.public: Who can play a game: everybody on Oomba Academy. Short, shown after 🌍.
status.hidden: Game status chip: hidden after players reported it. Shown after ⚠️.
status.inReview: Game status chip: waiting for a safety check. Shown after ⏳.
status.needsChanges: Game status chip: the reviewer asked for changes. Shown after ✏️.
status.suspended: Game status chip: switched off by the safety team. Shown after ⛔.
status.draft: Game status chip: not shared yet. Shown after 📝.
categories.arcade: Game category (chip and row title), one word if possible.
categories.board: Game category: board games (like chess, ludo). One word if possible.
categories.words: Game category: word games (spelling, word search). One word if possible.
categories.silly: Game category: funny, goofy games. One word if possible.
home.build.title: Heading of the banner on the home page that invites kids to make a game.
home.build.openStudio: Button, max ~18 chars. The Studio is where you make games.
home.rails.featured: Title of a row of games, max ~20 chars.
home.rails.playing: Title of a row of games people are playing at this moment, max ~20 chars.
home.rails.mine: Title of the row of games the player built.
home.hero.kicker: Small label above the big featured game on the home page.
home.hero.play: Big button that starts a game, max ~8 chars. Shown after ▶.
home.hero.more: Button that opens the game's page, max ~12 chars.
home.hero.about: Screen-reader label of the game picture link. {title} is the game title.
search.titleQuery: Browser tab title for a search. {text} is what was typed. Use your language's quotation marks.
search.placeholder: Search box hint. "shark" and "soccer" are example searches: translate them as words a kid would type.
search.sortLabel: Label before the sort buttons, max ~8 chars.
search.gameCount: {count} is how many games a builder made.
search.noMatch: {text} is what the kid typed. Use your language's quotation marks.
info.safety.heading: The Safety page is read by kids: keep it at a 7-year-old's reading level.
info.safety.chat.p2: "Me page" is the page behind the Me tab (nav.me): use the same word as nav.me.
info.safety.checked.p2: "🚩 Report" is the button on the game page (game.report): use the same word.
info.parents.heading: The For grown-ups page is read by parents and teachers: normal adult language is fine.
info.sdk.brb.p1: Developer page for kids who build games. {get} and {set} are code samples (BRB.storage.get(key) and BRB.storage.set(key, value)): keep them where they fit in your sentence. "localStorage" is a code word: do not translate it.
info.sdk.brb.p2: {submit} and {over} are code samples: keep them in the sentence.
info.sdk.brb.p3: {fx} is a long list of code samples (effects and sounds). "add juice" means: make a game feel lively and fun.
info.sdk.brb.p4: {full} and {orient} are code samples (full screen, turn sideways).
info.sdk.brb.p5: {lang} and {dir} are code samples. Keep "fr", "ar" and "rtl" as they are (they are codes).
info.sdk.rules.p1: Google Fonts and cdnjs are product names: keep them.
game.play: Big button that starts the game, max ~8 chars. Shown after ▶.
game.like: Small icon button under ❤️, max ~8 chars.
game.share: Small icon button under 🔗, max ~8 chars.
game.edit: Small icon button under 🛠️ (open the game in the Studio), max ~8 chars.
game.updateWaiting: Shown to the game's builder after the status, e.g. "🌍 Everyone · an update is waiting for review". Lowercase start if your language allows.
game.reviewer: {note} is a note the safety reviewer wrote (it may be in English).
game.stats.ratings: Small text under the average star number. {count} is the exact number of ratings (for the plural), {n} the same number shortened like "1.2K". Show {n}.
game.stats.noRatings: Small text under "New" when a game has no ratings.
game.stats.playingNow: Small label under a big number (people playing this game right now).
game.stats.plays: Small label under a big number: how many times it was played. {count} is that number (only used to pick the plural form, do not show it).
game.stats.likes: Small label under a big number of likes. {count} is that number (only used to pick the plural form, do not show it).
game.about.players: {count} is the most players that can play on one device (2 to 8).
game.about.sideways: The game works best with the phone turned sideways (landscape).
game.about.updated: {when} is a relative time like "5 minutes ago" or "yesterday", already translated.
game.rate.stars: Screen-reader label of each star button. {count} is 1 to 5.
game.rate.guest: Button for visitors who are not signed in yet.
game.report.button: Small icon button under 🚩 to tell the team something is wrong with a game, max ~8 chars.
game.report.reasons.grownup: Report reason: content for adults only, not for kids. Kid reading level.
game.report.reasons.copy: Report reason: the game copies somebody else's game or characters.
game.shareText.private: "Friends" and "Everyone" are the sharing choices (vis.friends, vis.public): use the same words.
game.api.badScore: Technical error a game may cause; rarely seen.
play.backTo: Screen-reader label of the Back button on the play screen. {title} is the game title.
play.rate: Icon button in the dark bar above a game, max ~8 chars.
play.fullScreen: Icon button in the dark bar above a game, max ~12 chars.
play.frameExpired: Plain text page shown if an old game link is opened.
play.defaultPlayer: Name a game shows for a player who is not signed in.
friends.playing: Under a friend's name. {game} is an emoji plus a game title, e.g. "🦈 Shark Plank" (not translated).
friends.code.heading: A friend code is a secret 6-character code each player has; friends type it to add you. Use one consistent term for "friend code" everywhere.
friends.waiting.heading: Heading for friend requests you sent that the other kid has not accepted yet.
friends.waiting.asked: {when} is a relative time like "5 minutes ago", already translated.
friends.api.tooManyTries: Shown after many wrong friend codes in a row (rate limit).
profile.description: Meta description of a public profile page. {name} is the display name. Keep "Oomba Academy" as is: the brand stays in Latin letters, untranslated.
profile.team: Badge for staff accounts. Keep "Oomba Academy" as is: the brand stays in Latin letters, untranslated.
profile.stats.games: Label under the number of games a builder made. {count} only picks the plural form (do not show it).
profile.beFriends: {link} becomes a link with the word for "Friends" (nav.friends). Keep {link} where the word fits in your sentence.
profile.badges.builder.label: Profile badges: label max ~12 chars; "why" is a tooltip that explains how you earn it.
profile.badges.hit.label: A badge for making a very popular game.
chat.offNotice: {link} becomes a link with the word for "Me" (nav.me). Keep {link} where it fits in your sentence.
chat.safety.text: Important safety advice for kids aged 6 to 12. Keep it simple and clear.
chat.inbox.sayHi: Shown under a friend's name in the chat list when you have not chatted yet.
chat.inbox.you: Preview of the last message in a chat when you sent it. {text} is that message.
chat.thread.game: Tiny label under the 🎮 button that shares a game, max ~6 chars.
chat.quick.hi: Quick chat phrases kids tap to send. Very short (max ~16 chars), friendly, keep the emoji. The friend sees the phrase in THEIR own language.
chat.quick.brb: "Be right back": use the usual short chat form in your language.
chat.cant.chat_off_me: "Me" is the Me tab (nav.me): use the same word.
chat.cant.blocked_by_me: "Friends page" is the Friends tab (nav.friends): use the same word.
chat.paused: {minutes} is a number of minutes. Shown after a kid sent several blocked messages.
chat.blocked.words: Shown when a chat message had a rude word and was not sent. Kind tone, not scolding.
chat.blocked.handle: A handle is a username on another app, like @someone.
build.newGame: Big button, max ~14 chars. Shown after ✨.
build.startFrom: Heading above ready-made starter games a kid can begin from.
build.startFromLabel: Screen-reader label of a starter card. {title} is the starter's name (studio.templates.*.title).
build.changed: {when} is a relative time like "5 minutes ago", already translated.
studio.title: Browser tab title. {title} is the game's name. "Studio" is the page where kids make games: pick one word and use it everywhere.
studio.newGameTitle: Default name of a brand-new game (the kid can rename it), max ~20 chars.
studio.startedFrom: Version-history note. {title} is a starter's name.
studio.status.live: Status chip. {who} is like "🌍 Everyone" (from vis.*).
studio.top.save: Small icon button under 💾, max ~10 chars.
studio.top.versions: Small icon button under 🕘 (list of earlier versions of the game), max ~10 chars.
studio.top.settings: Small icon button under ⚙️, max ~10 chars.
studio.top.publish: Main button: share the game so others can play it. Max ~12 chars. Shown after 🚀.
studio.chat.builder: The name of the AI helper that builds games. Use one consistent word everywhere (here, in chat, in the Builder's own replies).
studio.chat.pro: Toggle for a slower, better AI model. Max ~14 chars.
studio.chat.placeholder: Hint in the message box to the AI Builder.
studio.templates.quiz.title: Starter game names and descriptions on the Build page. Titles max ~24 chars.
studio.api.savedNote: Version-history note for a saved version. {note} is the name the kid typed (or studio.api.savedDefault).
studio.api.savedDefault: Used as the name of a saved version when the kid did not type one.
studio.api.restarting: "Server" = the computer that runs the website. Shown when a message is sent while the site restarts; the message is not lost.
builder.kindRefusal: The Builder (the AI helper) says this when it cannot help. Speaks as "I". Kid reading level, 7-year-old.
builder.scanStillFailing: “Ask the Builder to fix it” is a button label (js.studio.fixButton): use the same words.
builder.turnTimeout: Said by the Builder (as "I") when a build reached the time limit (20 minutes) after saving a version. Keep the ⏱️.
builder.turnTimeoutNothing: Like builder.turnTimeout, when nothing was saved: the turn was given back. "Turn" means one of the daily Builder turns.
builder.errors.tooMany: The 2 is fixed in the code. Friendly, not a telling-off.
builder.refusals.tryThese: Question above 3 tappable game ideas after a refusal.
builder.refusals.rules.message: The Builder's kind refusals. Speaks as "I", warm and never scolding, kid reading level (7-year-old). The "suggestion" always offers a fun alternative idea.
builder.refusals.rules.suggestion: The quoted game idea is an example: translate it.
builder.refusals.selfharm.message: Shown when a child mentions self-harm or wanting to die. Must be gentle, caring and point to a trusted grown-up. Keep the 💛.
builder.refusals.copyright.suggestion: "Zip" is a made-up name for a fox; you may pick a short fun name that works in your language (and use the same name in builder.refusals.chips.copyright.a).
builder.refusals.chips.copyright.a: Refusal chips are tappable game ideas that get sent to the Builder as a message. Keep each under ~30 chars and keep the emoji first.
uploads.badType: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, PDF, TXT, MD, CSV and JSON are file types: keep them as they are.
uploads.image.real_faces: Shown when a kid uploads a photo with a real person's face. Kind tone.
js.app.playing: Updated every 30 seconds on game covers. {n} is a number already formatted (maybe shortened like "1.2K"). Keep it very short.
js.app.justNow: Relative time for less than a minute ago (same as time.justNow).
js.game.needSignIn: Toast. “Play as guest” must match auth.page.playAsGuest (without the emoji).
js.game.unliked: Toast after tapping Like again to undo it.
js.game.holdToCopy: Shown when copying did not work: tell the kid to long-press the link to copy it.
js.play.newBest: Toast in the game screen. {score} is a number.
js.friends.playing: {game} is an emoji plus a game title (same as friends.playing).
js.chat.paused: Same meaning as chat.paused. {minutes} is a number.
js.studio.docTitle: Browser tab title (same as studio.title + " · Oomba Academy"). {title} is the game's name.
js.studio.turns: {left} and {total} are numbers: Builder messages a kid has left today.
js.studio.fixButton: Button that asks the AI Builder to fix safety problems, max ~28 chars. Shown after 🛠️.
js.studio.fixMessage: Sent as a chat message to the AI Builder, followed by the (English) list of problems. {number} is a version number.
js.studio.top.update: Main Studio button when a newer version can replace the live game. Max ~20 chars.
js.studio.top.live: Short status: the game is published and playable. Max ~8 chars.
js.studio.live.liveVersion: {number} is a version number, {who} is like "👫 Friends".
js.studio.live.playersOn: {live} and {number} are version numbers. “Update live game” must match js.studio.top.update.
js.studio.live.reviewer: {note} is the safety reviewer's note (often in English). "Update" and "Publish" are button names.
js.studio.safety.chipFlag: Tiny chip after ⚠️ (a person will check), max ~8 chars.
js.studio.log.namedIt: Shown in the Builder chat after the AI named the game. {title} is the game's name, shown in bold.
js.studio.log.hello: The AI Builder's first message. Speaks as "I". Kid reading level.
js.studio.log.readyToPlay: {title} is the game's name. Use your language's quotation marks.
js.studio.startChips.a: Tappable game ideas sent to the AI Builder as a message. Keep the emoji first, max ~32 chars each.
js.studio.nextChips.a: Tappable next-step ideas sent to the AI Builder, max ~30 chars each.
js.studio.settings.tags: Label for words that help people find the game in search.
js.studio.settings.tagsPlaceholder: Example search words for a shark game, with commas: translate them.
js.studio.settings.or.portrait: Screen direction: phone held upright. One short word.
js.studio.settings.or.landscape: Screen direction: phone turned on its side. One short word.
js.studio.covers.sunset: Names of card background colors, read by screen readers only. One word each.
js.studio.versions.bringBack: Button that restores an old version of the game, max ~14 chars.
js.studio.update.version: Used inside js.studio.update.text. {number} is a version number.
uploads.image.resting: Shown when a child uploads a picture while the AI spending cap is reached, so the picture can't be safety-checked. Kid reading level.
me.theme.heading: Me page panel with the theme choice, next to the Language panel.
auth.page.forgotOwn: Sign-in page, under the form. Keep it honest: there is no email recovery and no way to look a password up.
layout.notYou.signedInAs: On students' class, lesson and My classes pages (shared classroom devices). {name} is the player's display name, shown in bold.
layout.notYou.button: Small button after "Signed in as …", max ~24 chars. One tap signs out and opens the sign-in page.
me.password.hintStaff: {min} is a number of characters. For teachers and school admins.
me.password.staffShort: {n} is how many characters were typed (fewer than {min}), with plural forms; {min} is a number of characters. For teachers and school admins.
me.password.school: Shown to school-account students instead of the change-password form.
info.parents.ai.p1: For grown-ups. Keep "Claude" and "Anthropic" as they are: a product name and a company name.
auth.page.forgotSchool: Sign-in page, under the form. Students get new login cards from their teacher; teachers and other staff from their school admin.
layout.signedOut: Shown once at the top of the next page after a sign-in ended (timed out, or signed out on another device). Keep the … around the words that sign in again. Kid reading level, calm: nothing went wrong.
layout.shortPassword: Shown on every page to teachers, school admins and the platform admin whose password is shorter than {min} characters, until they change it. Keep the … around the words that open the change-password form. Adult reader.
js.app.signedOut: Pop-up or chat message when something was sent after the sign-in ended (timed out, or signed out on another device). Kid reading level, calm.
info.parents.contact.p1: For grown-ups. {email} is the team's email address (a link).
play.device.title: Inside a 3D game, when the phone, tablet or computer cannot show 3D (too old: no WebGL 2 or import maps). Big heading on a card, kid-friendly, max ~50 chars.
play.device.text: Under play.device.title: what to do instead (newer device, update the browser) and that there are other games. One or two short sentences.
play.device.lostTitle: Inside a 3D game when the 3D picture is lost (a GPU reset, memory pressure, coming back from the background) — happens on new devices too, not only old ones. Big heading on a card, kid-friendly, max ~40 chars.
play.device.lostText: Under play.device.lostTitle: says it sometimes happens and to tap the Try again button to start over. One or two short sentences.
play.device.retry: Label on a big button that reloads the game to start it over. Very short (1-2 words), e.g. "Try again".
studio.templates.island.title: Name of the 3D "Start from" template on the Build page: an island with stars to collect. Short, max ~22 chars.
studio.templates.island.description: One-line description of the 3D island template card on the Build page.
js.studio.vis.class: Sharing level in the Studio's share dialog (after 🎒): "My class" when the builder is in one class, "My classes" for several. Keep it short (~16 chars).
js.studio.share.classOne: Under "🎒 My class" when the builder is in exactly one class. {name} is the class name a teacher typed (e.g. "5B").
js.studio.share.classesLegend: Heading over the list of the builder's classes, each with a checkbox.
js.studio.share.allClasses: Checkbox label that ticks every class in the list.
js.studio.share.classInSchool: One class in the list when the builder is in classes at two schools. {class} is the class name, {school} the school name.
js.studio.share.classRemoved: Under a greyed-out class in the list: a teacher took this game off that class, so it can't be picked.
js.studio.live.sharedWith: Status line in the Studio. {names} is a list of class names already joined in the reader's language (e.g. "5B and Art Club").
js.studio.steps.title: Heading of the small card in the Builder chat that shows, step by step, what the Builder is doing. Short.
js.studio.steps.tipsOn: Button in that card, after 💡: the learning tips are shown. Max ~14 chars (same for tipsOff).
js.studio.steps.earlier: Button that shows the steps hidden above the latest ones. Shown after ▾.
js.studio.steps.summaryAi: One line on a phone (390 px), after 🧠. {time} is a duration the browser formats, like “1 min 24 sec”. “AI” here is the AI Builder.
js.studio.steps.summaryBlocks: Like summaryAi, for the simple building blocks (the non-AI fallback; same words as builder.budgetResting).
js.studio.steps.tokens: “Token” is the word AI people use for a small piece of a word. Keep it (or the usual word in your language) and explain it as in English. {read} and {wrote} are numbers.
js.studio.steps.loopAi: A “round” is one turn of the AI: it reads the chat and the game, thinks, then uses a tool. Use the same word for “round” in all think.* keys.
js.studio.steps.screen.learn: Learning lines (all *.learn keys): one short sentence for kids 8–12, at most about 20 words, simple words, warm, no hype. Shown under the step that is running. Keep them accurate: no extra claims.
js.studio.steps.blocks.now: “Simple building blocks” is the Builder's non-AI fallback. Use the same words as builder.budgetResting.
js.studio.steps.think.now.start: {n} is the round number. A round is one turn of the AI (see loopAi). Use the same word for “round” in all think.* keys and loopAi.
js.studio.steps.write.now: Step labels (*.now while the step runs, *.done after): short, fit one or two lines on a phone.
js.studio.steps.check.pass: “Safety program” is the automatic code checker, a normal program (not AI). Use one word for it in all check.* keys, think.learn.scan and facts.h. {v} is a version number.
js.studio.steps.name.title: {title} is the game's name (not translated). Use your language's quotation marks. {icon} is an emoji.
js.studio.steps.planLabel: Before the AI's own one-sentence plan for this step (written by the AI in the kid's language).
js.studio.steps.facts.a: “Did you know?” facts for kids 8–12. One or two short sentences each, at most about 20 words. Keep them accurate: no extra claims.
js.studio.steps.facts.e: 14 is a fixed number in the code (rounds per message). Keep it.
js.studio.steps.offline.now: Shown when the phone's connection to the Builder dropped mid-build; the Builder keeps working and the page waits for it.
js.studio.steps.srDone: Screen-reader only (srDone, srNow, srWarn): the state of a step. One or two words.
js.studio.steps.thinkingNow: Short word after 🤔, next to a round, while the AI thinks quietly before it answers (its thoughts are never shown). 1–2 lowercase words. thoughtFirst is the same once it has answered.
js.studio.steps.justNow: Lead-in before the learning line of a step that was over in a flash (like the safety program’s check), shown under the next step for a few seconds. Short.
js.studio.steps.srPaused: Screen-reader word on a step whose end is unknown because the connection dropped (the Builder may still be on it).
js.studio.steps.offline.check: The connection dropped before the page heard back from the Builder, so it is checking whether the message arrived. Kid reading level.
js.studio.steps.check.flag: {k} is how many things the safety program listed (1 or more): use the plural forms your language needs, and keep =1 for the one-thing wording. {v} is a version number.
js.studio.steps.showLess: Button at the bottom of the opened steps summary that folds it again. Shown after ▴. Short.
js.studio.steps.think.learn.start: Explains a “round” to kids: one time the app asks the AI. Use the same word for “round” as in the think.* labels and loopAi.
js.studio.steps.leave: Top of the live build card. 'Oomba Builder' is the product name: keep 'Oomba'. Must stay true: the build really goes on after closing the page or signing out. 'Close your computer' means shutting a laptop or turning a tablet off, said the way a child would.
js.studio.steps.restart.now: 'Server' = the computer that runs the website. Short; also shown as the status pill on the preview.
js.studio.steps.resume.doneV: {v} is a version number. A row in the live build steps card, past tense.
js.studio.steps.stopRestart: Ends the one-line summary of a build, after ' · ' (like js.studio.steps.stopped). Lower case start.
js.studio.steps.stopTime: Ends the one-line summary of a build, after ' · ' (like js.studio.steps.stopped). Lower case start.
js.studio.resumedV: {v} is a version number. A small note in the chat above the Builder’s reply.
js.studio.continue: Button under a build that stopped early: the Builder carries on with the same message. Max ~24 chars.
js.studio.continueMessage: Sent as the child’s chat message when they tap “Carry on building” (js.studio.continue).
js.studio.notCounted: 'Turn' as in js.studio.turns (the daily Builder turns).
js.studio.followups.putBack: Button: puts the message back in the typing box so it can be sent again. 'Box' = the message box.
build.status.building: A small chip on the 'My games' list. At most about 14 characters.
me.tiles.building: Small line under “My games” on the Me page. {count} is a number of games.
layout.build.ready: One-time note at the top of the next page. Keep the <a href="{href}"> link and {title}.
layout.build.many: One-time note at the top of the next page when several games have news. Keep the <a href="{href}"> link.
studio.api.liveBusy: The same game is open in many browser tabs at once.
errors.moved.text: Shown for a moment while the browser goes to the site's new address. {site} is the new address, like oomba.ai: keep it as is.
errors.moved.link: Link to the site's new address, in case the page doesn't move on by itself. {site} is the new address, like oomba.ai.
auth.page.moved: Sign-in page, after the site moved to a new address and the sign-in could not come along. {site} is the new address, like oomba.ai.
js.studio.steps.think.now.plan: Round 1 after the AI has read the message and is working out its answer (it may be thinking quietly). Same word for “round” as the other think.* labels.
js.studio.steps.think.learn.long: Shown when the first round has been planning for 45 seconds. Must stay true: the build continues after leaving the page.
js.studio.followups.gotAi: 'Step' as in the steps card. Shown in a small strip while the AI works.
js.studio.followups.turnNote: 'Turn' as in js.studio.turns (the daily Builder turns).
js.studio.steps.think.now.msg: 'Round' is the same word as in the other think.* keys.
builder.followUps.cap: Said by the Builder to a child aged 8–12. Friendly, not a telling-off. {max} is the number of extra messages allowed (3).
js.studio.followups.readingAi: Under a message the child sent while the AI works: the AI has just been given it.
js.studio.followups.placeholderAi: Placeholder in the message box while the AI builds. Must fit on one line of a wide box (about 55 characters); placeholderShort is used when it doesn’t fit.
js.studio.followups.placeholderShort: Short placeholder in the message box while the Builder builds, used on phones. Max ~22 characters, one line.
js.studio.followups.capPlaceholder: Placeholder in the message box once 3 extra messages were sent during a build (Send is off). About 45 characters; capShort is used when it doesn’t fit.
js.studio.followups.capShort: Short form of capPlaceholder for phones. Max ~22 characters, one line.
js.studio.eta.about: Shown at the top of the live build card while the Builder builds. {time} is a duration the browser writes in your language, like '2 minutes'. 'Usually' matters: it comes from timed builds and is not a promise.
js.studio.eta.range: {time} is a range the browser writes, like '2–3 minutes'. Don't add 'about'. 'Usually' matters, as in js.studio.eta.about.
js.studio.eta.guess: Shown while there aren't enough timed builds yet. {time} is written by the browser ('2 minutes', '1–2 minutes'). 'About' matters: it is a guess, so don't use the word for 'usually'.
js.studio.eta.soFar: After the estimate, on the same line. {time} is whole minutes the browser writes, like '1 minute'.
js.studio.eta.tailAbout: Shown right after the game was saved, while the Builder checks and finishes. {time} is whole minutes the browser writes, like '1 minute'.
js.studio.eta.tailGuessAbout: Like js.studio.eta.tailAbout, but while the time is still a guess: 'may', not 'usually'.
js.studio.eta.tailGuessUnder: Like js.studio.eta.tailUnder, but while the time is still a guess: 'may', not 'usually'.
js.studio.eta.longer: Replaces the estimate when the build takes longer than the time shown. Calm, not alarming.
js.studio.eta.big: Replaces js.studio.eta.longer when the build goes on much longer. Calm, not alarming.
js.studio.eta.newMsg: Shown after the Builder starts reading a message the child sent while it works.
js.studio.eta.learnAi: 'Tokens' as in js.studio.steps.tokens (small pieces of words). Learning line: one short sentence.
js.studio.eta.learnBlocks: 'Building blocks' as in js.studio.steps.blocks.now and builder.budgetResting. Learning line: one short sentence.
js.studio.resting.text: Shown in the Builder chat when the site's daily AI spending limit is reached. {when} is one of resting.today / resting.tomorrow / resting.date, already translated. Must stay true: turns are not used while it rests.
js.studio.resting.date: {date} is a weekday and date in the reader's language, like 'Saturday, Nov 1'. {time} is a clock time.
nav.family: Menu tab for grown-up (parent) accounts: their family page. Max ~10 chars (it fits under an icon in the phone tab bar).
layout.shortPasswordGrownup: For adults: notice at the top of every page for a parent's account with a short password. {min} is a number, {href} the link to the password form; keep the <a> tag.
me.password.hintGrownup: For adults: hint under the new-password field on a parent's account. {min} is a number (12).
me.family.heading: Kid page: heading of a small panel on the child's own Me page that lets a parent link to the account. Neutral: never mention money, plans or paying.
me.family.text: Kid page, plain words. Never mention money, plans or paying.
me.family.codeHow: Kid page. {where} is the web address a grown-up types the code at (e.g. oomba.ai/family/link); it is plain text, not a link.
me.family.codeWarn: Kid page, a safety line shown right under a new link code. Plain, calm words a 6-year-old can follow: give the code only to your own parent or guardian, in person; never in chat, in a game or online.
me.family.pending: Kid page, a safety question. Keep the <b> tags around "Your grown-up": it is a fixed label, never a name. Calm, clear words.
me.family.pendingCheck: Kid page, shown under me.family.pending. "Report" is the button label me.family.report: use the same word.
me.family.linked: Kid page. Keep the <b> tags; "your grown-up" is a fixed label, never a name.
me.family.report: Kid page: button to report a grown-up the child doesn't know. Short (one word if possible).
info.parents.families.h: For adults: section of the page for parents about grown-up (parent) accounts.
family.landing.description: For adults: meta description for search engines, max ~150 chars.
family.landing.what.p1: For adults. {extra} is a number of messages (plural form), {max} the number of children (4). Never write "per day".
family.landing.price.p1: For adults. {monthly} and {yearly} are prices already formatted in US dollars (e.g. "$7.99").
family.landing.price.us: For adults. Family plans can only be bought in the United States for now.
family.landing.how.p2: For adults. Keep the <b> tags; "Me", "For grown-ups" and "Get a code" must match the words the child sees (me.family.heading, me.family.getCode, nav.me).
family.landing.faq.reset.local: For adults. {time} is a clock time in the reader's own time zone, e.g. "7:00 PM".
family.landing.faq.consent.a: For adults. Legal wording: say only that linking and plans are not how consent is asked for or recorded. Never say that paying gives consent or verifies an adult.
family.signup.adult: For adults: a checkbox the parent ticks themselves (a statement, not a check).
family.signup.signedIn: For adults. {name} is the name of the account signed in on this device (already bold).
family.login.forgot: For adults. {email} is our support email address (a link).
family.page.pendingSent: For adults. {when} is a relative time like "5 minutes ago".
family.page.yesterday: For adults. {n} is a number of Builder messages. Shown before family.page.month, joined with " · ".
family.page.month: For adults. {n} is a number of Builder messages; it follows family.page.yesterday after " · ", so it starts in lower case in English.
family.page.removeConfirm: For adults: a confirmation box. {name} is the child's display name.
family.page.help: For adults. {email} is our support email address (a link).
family.page.off: For adults: shown on the grown-up's own page while family accounts are switched off on this site (only language, password and Sign out are there).
family.link.step1: For adults. Keep the <b> tags; "Me", "For grown-ups" and "Get a code" must match the words the child sees (nav.me, me.family.heading, me.family.getCode).
family.landing.title: For adults: everything under family.* is for parents and guardians (plain adult tone, never shown to children). Page title.
family.landing.what.limitDaily: For adults: one of the family plan's limits, stated before buying (not hidden). {daily} is a number of messages (plural form). Shown only when it is smaller than the monthly extras.
family.landing.what.limitCost: For adults: one of the family plan's limits (a cost backstop), stated before buying. Never name a dollar amount.
family.landing.what.limitReset: For adults: when the family's extra messages start again. "UTC" stays as is.
family.billing.password.label: For adults: label of the password field shown before a payment or plan change.
family.billing.password.hint: For adults. Says why the password is asked again (so a child on the same device can't buy anything).
family.billing.password.needed: For adults. Error when the password field was left empty.
family.billing.password.wrong: For adults. Error for a wrong password.
family.billing.manage: For adults: button that opens Stripe's page to change the card, switch monthly/yearly, see receipts or cancel. Max ~20 chars.
family.billing.welcome: For adults: short confirmation after paying (a toast).
family.billing.waiting: For adults: shown after coming back from the payment page while the plan is being switched on.
family.billing.slow: For adults: shown when the plan isn't on a minute after paying.
family.billing.back: For adults: link under family.billing.slow back to the grown-up's own page.
family.billing.grant: For adults. {date} is a date, e.g. "Oct 24, 2026".
family.billing.pastDue: For adults. {date} is a date. "Manage billing" must match family.billing.manage.
family.billing.extrasLeft: For adults. {left} and {total} are numbers (plural form on {total}). Never write "per day". Counted up to the end of yesterday (UTC), so the page never shows what a child is doing right now.
family.billing.extrasReset: For adults. {date} is the 1st of next month.
family.billing.terms.renew: For adults: automatic-renewal notice shown right before paying (required by law). Keep it clear and complete.
family.billing.terms.cancel: For adults: cancellation notice shown before paying. "Manage billing" must match family.billing.manage.
family.billing.terms.refund: For adults: the refund policy in one line. Keep "14 days", "first payment" and "yearly renewal" exact.
family.billing.terms.agree: For adults. {terms} is a link whose text is family.billing.terms.link.
family.billing.terms.link: For adults: link text to the Terms of Service page.
family.billing.subscribeMonthly: For adults: button. {price} is a price already formatted in US dollars, e.g. "$7.99".
family.billing.subscribeYearly: For adults: button. {price} is a price already formatted in US dollars, e.g. "$69.00".
family.billing.stripe: For adults. Keep "Stripe" as is (a company name).
family.billing.history: For adults. "Manage billing" must match family.billing.manage.
family.billing.errors.entitled: For adults. "Manage billing" must match family.billing.manage.
family.billing.errors.fixPayment: For adults: shown instead of Subscribe while the family's plan waits for a payment. "Manage billing" must match family.billing.manage.
builder.errors.limitToday: For kids: the Builder's limit message when no number is shown. Never mention plans, paying or grown-ups.
js.studio.extra: For kids: next to the Studio's message counter, max ~22 chars. {n} is a number. Never mention plans, paying or grown-ups.
builder.errors.limitClass: For kids: the Builder's message when a school student has no messages left today. No numbers, plans or money words.
js.studio.turnsLeftToday: For kids: the Studio's message counter in class, max ~16 chars. {left} is a number of Builder messages. Never a total, plan or money words.
school.tabs.billing: Tab of the school page for school admins, max ~12 chars: the school plan and payments.
school.errors.badCap: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Error for the daily Builder messages setting. {min} and {max} are numbers (the lowest is the free daily messages).
school.billing.heading: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Heading of the Billing tab.
school.billing.none: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.active: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {count} is the number of paid students.
school.billing.renews: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {date} is a date, e.g. "Oct 24, 2027".
school.billing.ends: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {date} is a date.
school.billing.grant: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {date} is a date, {count} a number of students. Keep "Oomba Academy" as is.
school.billing.pastDue: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {date} is a date.
school.billing.overdue: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {date} is a date.
school.billing.invoiceOpen: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {amount} is a price in US dollars, {date} a date.
school.billing.invoiceView: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Link to Stripe's invoice page. Max ~16 chars.
school.billing.pool: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {left} and {total} are numbers, {date} the end of the billing year. The pool the whole school shares.
school.billing.lessons: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {count} is a number. A Builder lesson: one class session where every student builds with the Builder (about 10 messages each).
school.billing.poolWaits: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.over: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {students} is "N students" (school.billing.studentsN), {seats} a number.
school.billing.studentsN: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {count} is a number.
school.billing.daily: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {cap} is a number.
school.billing.price: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {price} is a price in US dollars; {min} and {perSeat} are numbers.
school.billing.asyncFailed: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.pending: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.notOpen: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.waiting: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Shown after coming back from the payment page.
school.billing.welcome: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Short confirmation after paying (also a toast).
school.billing.slow: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.back: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Link, max ~20 chars.
school.billing.help: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {email} is the support email address (a link).
school.billing.seatsLabel: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Form label.
school.billing.seatsHint: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {min} is a number; {students} is "N students" (school.billing.studentsN).
school.billing.pay.heading: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Heading, max ~24 chars.
school.billing.pay.renew: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.pay.cancel: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).
school.billing.pay.tax: For school admins (adults; billing for the school).

school.billing.renewal.heading: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Heading, max ~20 chars.

school.billing.renewal.next: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {seats} is "N students" (school.billing.studentsN).
school.billing.renewal.hint: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). {min} is a number.
school.billing.renewal.button: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Button, max ~26 chars.

layout.footer.terms: Footer link to the Terms of Service page (/terms). Short.
layout.footer.privacy: Footer link to the Privacy Policy page (/privacy). Short.
info.legal.updated: Shown under the heading of the Terms, Refunds and Privacy pages. {date} is a date already written in your language.
info.legal.notYet: For adults. Shown on the Terms, Refunds and Privacy pages until paid plans are on sale.

info.refunds.heading: The Refund and Cancellation Policy page. Legal page for adults (parents, guardians, school admins): normal adult language, close to the English meaning. info.privacy.heading: The Privacy Policy page. Legal page for adults (parents, guardians, school admins): normal adult language, close to the English meaning. info.terms.plans.li20: OOMBA ACADEMY is the exact text on bank statements: keep it in Latin capitals.
info.terms.ai.li1: Keep "Claude" and "Anthropic" as they are: a product name and a company name.
info.privacy.payments.p1: Keep "Stripe, Inc." and the link text stripe.com/privacy as they are.

info.parents.stored.paid3: For grown-ups. Added to What we keep once paid plans are on sale.
info.safety.ads.paid1: Read by kids (7-year-old reading level). Replaces info.safety.ads.p1 once paid plans are on sale.
info.parents.plans.h: For grown-ups (/parents, shown only once paid plans are on sale). Section heading: the plans families and schools can buy. Short.
info.parents.plans.p1: For grown-ups (/parents). The site's one plans sentence: building is free, families and schools can buy extra Builder messages. No prices, no plan names.
info.parents.plans.p2: For grown-ups (/parents). Keep the three <a href> links and their addresses exactly; translate only the link words (the page names).
info.privacy.more.h: Privacy page, shown to signed-out visitors instead of the billing sections. Heading of a short pointer to the full policy. Short. No plan names.
info.privacy.more.p1: Privacy page, signed-out visitors. Points to the full policy (?for=grownups). Keep the <a href> and its address exactly. No plan names: children can read this page.
family.billing.legal: For grown-ups (/grown-ups and the family plan box on /family). Keep both <a href> links and their addresses exactly; translate only the page names.
school.billing.legal: For school admins (adults; billing for the school). Under the Pay by card and Request an invoice forms. Keep the three <a href> links and their addresses exactly; translate only the page names.
